title: Integration of symmetric cubic cocycles on disjoint subsets
statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set] and let $A$ be a commutative group, written multiplicatively with identity $1$ and inverses (multiplication is associative and commutative, $1a=a$, and $a^{-1}a=1$). Let $t(U,V,W)\in A$ be specified for every ordered triple of pairwise disjoint subsets of $E$. Assume that $t$ is invariant under all permutations of its three arguments, that $t(U,V,W)=1$ whenever at least one argument is empty, and that for every four pairwise disjoint subsets $U,V,W,Z\subseteq E$ one has
$$t(U,V,Z)t(U\cup V,W,Z)=t(V,W,Z)t(U,V\cup W,Z).$$
Then there is a function $c:\mathcal P(E)\to A$, with $c(B)=1$ for $|B|\leq2$, such that for every three pairwise disjoint subsets $U,V,W\subseteq E$,
$$t(U,V,W)=\frac{c(U\cup V\cup W)c(U)c(V)c(W)}{c(U\cup V)c(U\cup W)c(V\cup W)}.$$
Here $\mathcal P(E)$ is the set of all subsets of $E$, and division means multiplication by inverses. No divisibility or torsion restriction is imposed on $A$.

proof.text: Use strong induction on $|E|$, with finiteness as in [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set]. If $|E|\leq2$, set $c(B)=1$ for every $B$: any three pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets would contain three distinct elements, so every admissible triple has an empty argument and both sides equal $1$. For $|E|\geq3$, choose $x\in E$ and put $F=E\setminus\{x\}$. Restrict $t$ to subsets of $F$; all symmetry, normalization and cocycle hypotheses remain valid, so the induction hypothesis gives $c_0:\mathcal P(F)\to A$, equal to $1$ on sets of size at most two, with the required cubic formula on $F$.

proof.text:
For disjoint $U,V\subseteq F$ put $q(U,V)=t(U,V,\{x\})$. It is symmetric and normalized by the corresponding assumptions on $t$. Substituting the four disjoint blocks $U,V,W,\{x\}$ in the given identity gives
$$q(U,V)q(U\cup V,W)=q(V,W)q(U,V\cup W).$$
Apply [lem-sfb-disjoint-symmetric-two-cocycle-integration] to the finite set $F$ and the same commutative group $A$. Obtain $b:\mathcal P(F)\to A$ with $b(B)=1$ for $|B|\leq1$ and $q(U,V)=b(U\cup V)/(b(U)b(V))$ for disjoint pairs.

proof.text: Define $c(B)=c_0(B)$ if $x\notin B$, and $c(B)=c_0(B\setminus\{x\})b(B\setminus\{x\})$ if $x\in B$. These cases cover every subset uniquely. If $|B|\leq2$ and $x\in B$, the deleted set has size at most one, so both factors are $1$; if $x\notin B$, use the normalization of $c_0$. For a disjoint triple whose union avoids $x$, the formula for $c$ is the formula for $c_0$.

proof.text:
Otherwise symmetry lets us write the triple as $(U,V,Z\cup\{x\})$ with $U,V,Z\subseteq F$ pairwise disjoint. Substitution of step 3 in the seven-factor quotient defining the desired cubic difference cancels to
$$\frac{c_0(U\cup V\cup Z)c_0(U)c_0(V)c_0(Z)}{c_0(U\cup V)c_0(U\cup Z)c_0(V\cup Z)}\,
\frac{b(U\cup V\cup Z)b(Z)}{b(U\cup Z)b(V\cup Z)}
=t(U,V,Z)\frac{q(U\cup Z,V)}{q(Z,V)}.$$
Here the first factor is the induction formula and the second equality substitutes the two formulas for $q$ from step 2 and cancels $b(V)$. The original identity with four blocks $(U,Z,\{x\},V)$, followed by symmetry, is
$$t(U,V,Z)q(U\cup Z,V)=q(Z,V)t(U,V,Z\cup\{x\}).$$
Divide by $q(Z,V)$ to obtain the required equality. These identities also allow empty $U,V,Z$, so every triple is covered. This completes the induction without taking any roots in $A$.
